title: Anubhavanivedana — Report of Spiritual Experience
author: Abhinavagupta
text:
The Anubhavanivedana is a brief hymn of four verses in which Abhinavagupta, the supreme master of the Trika tradition of Kashmir (fl. c. 950–1016), reports the state handed to him by his own guru: mind and vital wind dissolved in the inward aim, sight steady yet seeing nothing external — the śāmbhavī mudrā, the gesture of pure consciousness, attained by grace alone. It belongs to the tradition of texts that transmit not an argument but an accomplished condition, and it does so in the first person, as testimony.

Its juice: the method here is explicitly none. What is described is consciousness already settled in itself, and the hymn's claim is that such a state is given, not manufactured — the guru's grace being the only cause that need be named.
